These controls distinguish observations from unsupported security claims.

- escaped-json.js matches dense-backslash-escape-triples: ordinary serialized
  JSON is a representation property, not concealed execution.
- geometry-host.js matches named-variable-call-assignment: host is a geometric
  segment, so variable spelling cannot prove URL construction.
- tenant-record.js matches tenant-id-token: tenant vocabulary alone is not OAuth.
- plain-record.js matches none of those observations; String conversion is
  excluded from the call-assignment matcher.

Matchers and scopes are preserved during relocation. The two exact escape
consumers now use the metadata ID. The call-assignment consumer in HTTP proxy
and the ABI co-occurrence composite use the source declaration ID; descriptions state
co-occurrence rather than data flow. The ABI composite moves to ABI decoding with its matcher.
No external exact references to the tenant token existed. Searches of active
YAML found no parent selectors of buffer/carve, HTTP URL build, or OAuth that
require changes; existing broad source declaration and metadata selectors were reviewed.
The staged-rotating-concealment/two-stage-cloaked.html fixture verifies both
hostile consumers still match. Sample scans and source facts are retained in
scratch beside the unpacked files, outside the traits repository.

All three original tarballs were SHA-256 verified and rescanned successfully.
Every member is a regular file, with no traversal names or link targets. No
package declares an install lifecycle hook. Source maps parse as version 3.
The query builder emits SQL and serializes query graphs; its escaped source
repository graph was decoded and contains type metadata, not executable code.
The IFC creator emits STEP model text and edits in-memory entity records; its
host variable stores a segment projection. Tenancy applies tenant predicates,
verifies request tenant selection, binds PostgreSQL transaction-local settings,
and generates reversible RLS migration SQL. No hostile behavior was found.
Atomscan records flow-analysis limitations, addressed here by manual source
inspection rather than treating missing flow facts as evidence of safety.

Fixture ID assertions follow the relocated call-binding ID. Two benign score
caps increase by one because source declarations now form a separate scoring
category from HTTP URL observations; no hostile/suspicious cap is relaxed.
